# Per-project idle-workbench report in the web console

## Description

This epic delivers a per-project idle-workbench report in the RHOAI web
console. Cluster administrators can see, for each project, which workbenches
are idle: each entry shows the workbench's last activity, its owner, and its
reserved resources (volumes and compute reservations). The report is sourced
from the notebook controller's existing activity tracking — the data already
exists and is only being surfaced, so no notebook-controller code changes are
in scope. Administrators can also export the report as CSV.

## Scope

- New idle-workbench report view in the web console, scoped per project
- Each listed workbench shows last activity timestamp, owner, and reserved
  resources, sourced from the notebook controller's activity tracking
- CSV export of the idle-workbench report for administrators
- Surface the report through the console's existing navigation and
  configuration conventions
- No automated reclamation or deletion of idle resources (out of scope per
  strategy)
- No cost/chargeback calculations (out of scope per strategy)

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a project containing workbenches with varying activity, when an
  administrator opens the idle-workbench report for that project, then every
  workbench in the project is listed with its last activity, owner, and
  reserved resources, measured by matching the report rows against the
  notebook controller's tracked activity data for the same project.
- Given a project with no workbenches, when an administrator opens the
  idle-workbench report, then an appropriate empty state is shown.
- Given the idle-workbench report, when an administrator exports it as CSV,
  then the CSV contains one row per workbench shown in the report with the
  same columns, measured by a round-trip comparison of exported rows to
  displayed rows.
- The notebook controller requires no code changes for this report; its
  existing activity tracking is consumed read-only (passive-component
  validation).

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P1): per-project idle-workbench report (last activity, owner,
  reserved resources) sourced from the notebook controller's activity
  tracking.
- HLR-3 (P2, this epic's share): CSV export of the idle-workbench report.

# Stale pipeline-run report in the web console

## Description

This epic delivers a per-project stale pipeline-run report in the RHOAI web
console. Cluster administrators can see completed pipeline runs older than a
configurable age threshold that still retain artifacts, so they can identify
runs whose retained storage is reclaimable. The report is sourced from
Kubeflow Pipelines' existing run completion metadata — no Kubeflow Pipelines
code changes are in scope. Administrators can also export the report as CSV.

## Scope

- New stale pipeline-run report view in the web console, scoped per project
- Lists completed pipeline runs older than a configurable age threshold,
  including an indication of retained artifacts, sourced from Kubeflow
  Pipelines run metadata
- The staleness age threshold is configurable; the configuration surface is
  decided by the implementing team
- CSV export of the stale pipeline-run report for administrators
- Surface the report through the console's existing navigation and
  configuration conventions
- No automated reclamation or deletion of runs or artifacts (out of scope per
  strategy)
- No cost/chargeback calculations (out of scope per strategy)

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a project containing completed pipeline runs of varying ages, when an
  administrator opens the stale pipeline-run report with a given age
  threshold, then only completed runs older than the threshold are listed
  with their retained artifacts, measured by matching the report rows against
  Kubeflow Pipelines run metadata for the same project.
- Given a changed staleness age threshold, when the report is re-rendered,
  then the filtered set of runs reflects the new threshold.
- Given the stale pipeline-run report, when an administrator exports it as
  CSV, then the CSV contains one row per pipeline run shown in the report
  with the same columns, measured by a round-trip comparison of exported rows
  to displayed rows.
- Kubeflow Pipelines requires no code changes for this report; its existing
  run completion metadata is consumed read-only (passive-component
  validation).

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-2 (P1): stale pipeline-run report (completed runs older than a
  configurable age with retained artifacts) sourced from Kubeflow Pipelines
  run metadata.
- HLR-3 (P2, this epic's share): CSV export of the stale pipeline-run report.

# Documentation for idle and stale resource reports and safe reclamation

## Description

This epic delivers Red Hat documentation explaining the two new console
reports — the per-project idle-workbench report and the stale pipeline-run
report — and the steps administrators can take to reclaim capacity safely.
This is substantive content authoring (new documentation topics), not
incidental touch-ups to existing pages.

## Scope

- New documentation topics explaining the idle-workbench report: what it
  shows (last activity, owner, reserved resources), where to find it, and
  that its data comes from the notebook controller's activity tracking
- New documentation topics explaining the stale pipeline-run report: what it
  shows (completed runs older than the configured age with retained
  artifacts), where to find it, and how to configure the staleness age
  threshold
- Guidance on safe reclamation steps for administrators (manual reclamation
  of idle workbenches and stale run artifacts), including appropriate caveats
- Explicit statement of what is not provided: no automated reclamation or
  deletion, no cost/chargeback calculations
- Screenshots and examples reflecting the shipped console behavior

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given the shipped reports, when the documentation is reviewed, then both
  the idle-workbench report and the stale pipeline-run report are explained
  with accurate descriptions of their columns, data sources, and the
  configurable staleness age, measured by technical review against the
  implemented console behavior.
- Given an administrator reading the documentation, when they follow the
  reclamation guidance, then the steps are safe to execute and consistent
  with the console's capabilities, measured by technical review confirming no
  guidance relies on automated reclamation (which is out of scope).
- Documentation is technically reviewed against the implemented reports
  before publication.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-4 (P2): documentation explains the reports and safe reclamation steps.

## Criterion Details

### 1. HLR Coverage (2/2)
All four HLRs map to at least one epic and the traceability matrix is present
and accurate. HLR-1 → E001, HLR-2 → E002, HLR-4 → E003; HLR-3 (P2, CSV export)
is deliberately bundled into E001 and E002 with an explicit coupling

priority collapse of a distinct deferrable feature. Priority inheritance is
correct: E001/E002 are P1 with no blocking epic below them; E003 is a
docs-authoring epic exempt from priority inheritance, and its P2 correctly
derives from the strategy's `priority: Normal`.

### 2. DAG Coherence (2/2)

matches frontmatter exactly: E003 depends on [E001, E002]; E001 and E002 have
empty dependencies, consistent with the documented no-edge justification
(independent backends, no shared data structures or API surfaces). Both edges
are Rule 11 (implementations → docs-authoring) edges, which are valid and do
not trigger priority inheritance. No konflux-onboarding, license-validation, or
repo-onboarding epics exist, so the mandated-parallelism rules (7, 8, 10) are
not applicable. Critical path length 2 is appropriate for an S-size strategy
(one active component, four HLRs). No conditional branch files are used and no
epic content reveals a data/artifact dependency missing from the DAG — the
passive components (Notebooks, Data Science Pipelines) are consumed read-only
with no epic of their own.

### 3. Epic Boundaries (2/2)
Component/team tuples are cleanly separated: E001 and E002 (Dashboard / RHOAI
Dashboard) and E003 (Documentation / RHOAI Documentation, an assumption flagged
as a health warning). No scope duplication: E001 and E002 each build a distinct
report against a distinct data source, and each handles only its own report's
CSV export — the overlap is incidental (shared navigation conventions), not
duplicate construction of the same surface. Work-product types are correctly
separated: code implementation lives in E001/E002, content authoring in E003.
No epic exceeds roughly two weeks of work.

### 4. Type Correctness (2/2)
No Investigation epics — justified: the strategy declares "Open Questions:
None" and contains no risks, assumptions, or conditional decisions. The one
candidate unknown (how the Dashboard reads notebook-controller activity data)
is reasonably handled as an acceptance criterion plus a health warning rather
than an Investigation, since the strategy asserts the data exists and the
outcome would not change which epics exist, only E001's internal scope. All
three epics are Implementation and produce concrete artifacts (two report
views, one documentation set). `gated_by` is null everywhere and no epic lists
an Investigation in dependencies, so gating metadata is trivially consistent.

### 5. AI Implementability Scoring (2/2)
Each epic is typed Implementation and carries `ai_signals` (the 9-signal
rubric) with `investigation_signals: null` — the type-appropriate field is
used. Frontmatter signal values match the ai-signals rationale files exactly,
and rationales are substantive and grounded in the strategy and architecture
context (e.g., repo_access +1 citing the public odh-dashboard repo;
architecture_claims +1 corroborated by the Notebooks and Data Science
Pipelines context files). E003's negative human_process_gates (-1, docs content
process plus mandatory technical review) is well justified. One borderline
value noted as a minor issue below; it does not contradict the rubric.

Every epic has testable Given/When/Then acceptance criteria derived from the
strategy, including measurement approaches (row-matching against source data,
CSV round-trip comparison). The docs-authoring epic carries the rule-mandated
technical-review AC ("Documentation is technically reviewed against the
implemented reports before publication"). No replacement epics exist (no
rollback/feature-flag AC required) and no konflux chain exists (no build
pipeline AC required). No epic body references sibling epics by draft ID.

### 7. Completeness (2/2)
All strategy scope is accounted for: both reports with their required fields
(HLR-1: last activity, owner, reserved resources; HLR-2: configurable age,
retained artifacts), CSV export for both reports (HLR-3), and documentation
covering both reports plus safe reclamation guidance with explicit caveats
(HLR-4). The strategy's out-of-scope statements (no automated reclamation, no
cost/chargeback) are carried into all three epic scopes. Secondary details are
covered: empty state for projects without workbenches, threshold-change
re-rendering, screenshots in docs. Strategy-level context (the passive
data-exposure risk and the unspecified configuration surface) is carried
forward as health warnings and ACs rather than silently dropped. No conditional
branches are used, and none are needed — the strategy has no bounded outcome
uncertainty.
